name: Project Zomboid
review:
I had a lot of fun in build 41 although once you learn how to fight or lure hordes the game does become fairly easy even though any tiny mistake you make at any time could cost your life. Which is fine because the game does expect you to die. Which is why build 42 makes no sense at all.

Build 42 is basically a completely different game. First: they have massively nerfed the player in combat. With the new muscle fatigue mechanic and the fact that zombies now move at different speeds it has became a far more tedious process to deal with zombies, especially hordes of 20-30, as you can not simply lure them away anymore. Secondly loot has been completely nerfed into the ground. Using rosewood as an example in build 41 you can go over to the second story apartments by the church and walk out with easily 20-30 cans of food and other goodies from the fridge. You could then walk down the bookstore and be greeted with 10-15 skill books per shelf and then proceed to loot the surrounding houses for even more canned food, enough to last you for months. In build 42....... those aparments MIGHT have 1-2 cans of food. Those shelves in the bookstore are barren or only have 2-3 literature or magazines on them. MAYBE 1 skill book, maybe, if you're lucky.  Houses are often so barren they aren't even worth looting anymore. For a game that expects you to die and has the ability to kill you over any tiny little mistake you make (even been scratched by a zombie once runs the risk of being infected) they expect you to deal with these layers of extreme tedium.

Surely there was a middle ground between build 41 and build 42. While I agree build 41 can be a little too easy when you know what you're doing build 42 seems like its doing everything it can to make the game as tedious, time consuming, and annoying as possible but still punishing you with death over any little microscopic mistake you make. Of course you can always just use sandbox mode and edit/change most of these settings to be a non issue however I believe the base experience (which is the experience most new players are going to get) should be enjoyable. 

Build 42 hates you and your time.

name: Project Zomboid
review:
I have never played a game for 300 hours and felt like not only did i gain absolutely nothing from the experience, but i also somehow got worse at the game the longer i played. Unfortunately i am probably going to keep playing. This is a game to play when youre angry and want to become more angry. The running into zombies and making your character spin and flip in every direction has killed so many runs. In game lore, the zombie apocalypse has literally just started and is still being reported and refuted on the news. Why is EVERY car you come across dilapidated and shitty and none of them have gas??? What the hell happened 10 minutes before the game takes place to make every vehicle like this??? Having gasoline be a valuable resource, the thing that runs vehicles and generators, what do you DO after the gas is gone/gone bad? Just cut wood and hunt rabbits forever? Theres no end to the game, no way to reach a credit scene, no NPCs, no real goal at all other than "haha youre gonna die :) you think you wont but youre going to die." And like i said about gas going bad/empty, same happens with the electricity and water supply. Which is cool and realisitc and all, but like, theres no goal at all?? No "survive 1 year and evac from Louisville" or "activate and repair radio towers to call for help" or "search military bases for radio frequencies or plans" or "clear every town to let the population grow" or anything??? just start the game with the lights on, then the lights go off, then you have to boil water, then you have to walk every where in absolute pitch black darkness and hoard batteries for flashlights, and find clothes that arent fucked so your character doesnt freeze to death in the winter and die of dysentary or other non zombie illness? Its trying to be a minecraft kinda thing where you make your own adventure, but it just gets harder and more impossible as time goes on, and shit doesnt happen and shit will never happen besides pushing zombies over and stomping their heads? But guess what???, youre physically exhausted from running, ridiculously sleepy tired because your characters have nightmares every night you dont have a cigarette before bed so you cant sleep more than 2 hours, you tore your leg open hopping over a fence, youre over encumbered because the game refuses to spawn you a bag, youre dehydrated because everytime you try to jump into a house for a drink you get chased out by zombies that attract every zombie on the block, and last but not least youre "extremely uncomfortable" for some fucking reason, so stomping a zombies head takes up to 17 stomps to kill them, which wakes up the whole neighborhood and has every zombie youve ever spared or ignored break into your windows like seal team 6 and just ruin you.

Or the game just wont register you pushing a zombie because your cursor is just a little too far away from the zombie, so your character animation pushes the zombie and makes contact, but because you were "technically aiming behind the zombie" in the fucked up isometric game with worse camera angles than resident evil, So now you did everything correct, had the right reaction time and everything, but because the games camera angles are dogshit, you just got bit by a singular zombie with no other zombies around for miles, and your run is over. Done,

 "why cant you just go back and pick up your stuff, or start a base?" reread my first paragraph. Time is valuable in this game, its not minecraft where you just go back and pick your stuff up, every second you waste going back to pick up your dropped loot is time against you, gasoline going bad/getting looted, houses getting looted by invisible nonexistant npcs that wont be added til well after gta6 has come out on the next 4 generations of consoles, water getting turned off, electricity getting turned off, and since the last update, the darkness is literally just pitch black screen. No moonlight, nothing. So if you cant get a decent run going and get a generator in time, its insanity. going back for your loot is just cutting a day off your available time with what little resources you have, and lets be real. everyone starts a new game once they die/get bit. and if you dont youre a pussy.

"but it realism"
But its a video game, made for entertainment and i should be having fun, not actually getting stressed out in real life by having to micromanage my characters health when theres no real reason to, theres no goals or endings or story or anything resembling fun to be had. Its literally just a sandbox for you to spawn in, struggle as hard as you possibly can, then watch time and time again as it all crumbles down. 

Theres dna for a great game here, however, This does just seem to somehow be a 14 year old unfinished, early access beta. Until some endgame content or npcs or anything at all gets added, this is getting a thumbs down

Even in the early access state, I do see Lethal Company as a rather complete game. For the quality and resolution wise, its not crisp and clear. However, I believe that the quality of the game makes up for it. A game of exploration, but yet the thrill you get does not exhaust so fast. Coupled with friends, I am assured that this game will not let you down.

Additionally, the game has constantly making progresses and updates, adding new maps and creatures. This normally should not be a compliment, but it is very assuring to see an Early Access game actually pushing for updates, and not some games, who simply claims to commit to the game just to simply abandon it months later without any news.

This game should not just be regarded as an early access game, because I believe it already has surpassed that when they have just released the game.

name: Red Dead Redemption 2
review:
i HIGHLY RECOMMEND. this game will CHANGE YOUR LIFE. 

holy smokes dude i don't think i can do rdr2 justice when explaining how beautiful of a game this is. the amount of content in this game is outrageous, in a good way. it's a perfect amount of grinding if you want to 100% it. not to mention, after story mode, you can move onto red dead online. red dead redemption 2 is the perfect game for you if you have too much free time. got this on sale for 15 usd and i feel like i've just bought 10 games in one.

rockstar has come up with every single possibility for any interaction with another, honestly i don't think i've even heard of every type of conversation you can have with another character, both camp members and strangers. you stand around waiting too long? they say something. sing too many songs at camp celebrations? your arthur will actually sing those tunes on his own! if you're away from camp for too long, theres a chance a camp member will come out scouting for you (this takes almost weeks of real-life time). one of my FAVORITE interactions is when you hold your gun up to a blind beggar in saint denis and they start panicking-- i thought you couldn't see? its also really funny when you get arthur heavily drunk and walk around town. 

in every playthrough, it'll be something different. you can play this game consistently for YEARS and still discover something new. it will NEVER EVER get old, its timeless. my recommendation is to play completely different each time. maybe youll do a low-honor playthrough by doing immoral deeds and next time, you'll become a selfless nomad, refusing to take money from others. seeing the details slightly differ depending on who you are as a person shows how thoughtful the devs were.

by now, rdr2 is nearing 7 years and the graphics are still amazing, especially for an open world game. its consistent. the huge variety of terrain and biomes makes this game so realistic. they blend together so well, it's quite literally a playable movie. genuinely one of the most realistic games i've played, i honestly wouldnt have been able to tell this was a videogame if you put it side-by-side to a photo of a real forest. its one of those games where you have to sit down, let out a heavy sigh, and just watch the sun set. 

you can also tell the developers did their research on the wild west. im no historian but this is crazy accurate to real-world, post-american civil war times and at unbelievable degrees, too. (a man with a kill-count of thousands might not be very accurate though...) 

story is pretty well-paced in MY books-- not too slow, not too fast. (personally, i like slower games) of course, it's up to the player to decide how they want to proceed. you could finish the whole game in a week or you can take your time, find new mechanics, complete stranger missions, or monopolize the animal kingdom. (correct me if im wrong but i think rdr2 has the most types of animals in any videogame). i love how you can do anything from gambling to herding sheep to playing dress up. 

super fun combat. its not hard at all. i like how they implemented the dead-eye mechanic. i haven't finished the first red dead redemption but i do think the first game's dead eye is better. regardless, still a cool feature. 

warning: you WILL cry when going through the story. but you'll also probably gasp for breath after laughing your ass off. theyve made each character so charming and utterly human. the storyline really touches your heart. not trying to spoil though. loved it more than anything. honestly? my second favorite game of all time. i am SUCH a sucker for open world (and sandbox-like) games. i love being able to do absolutely anything i can imagine. the beautiful story really ties the package together, i don't think there'll ever be a game that can outdo red dead redemption 2 in terms of being all-rounded. this game is so deeply rooted into my soul, i have this urge to just play it, experience it, everyday, for the rest of my damn life. 

i haven't indulged in mods but i know they can be game changers for some people. also, i play on a hp victus gaming laptop with an amd ryzen 5 series 5000, nvidia geforce gtx 1650, 16 gb ram. runs at 60 fps consistently (just play around with visuals a bit). my graphics card is usually maxed out while playing but thats not a big issue. just make sure those fans are clean so your computer doesnt combust and overheat.

100000000000/10 i'll probably force my next three generations to play this game, even just once.

Oh my Lord where do I even start with this game...

I could probably make a 2 hour video on JUST detailing all of the amateur graphical and UI errors the game has. There are actual blatant grammatical errors and strangely worded descriptions all over the whole UI.

This is on top of the insane air-vehicle bias, bad performance, ugly forced TAA making everything a blurry ghosting smudge, NO WAY to turn off ADS depth of field without messing around in the config file (what even???), mouse input that's actually steering a virtual joystick instead of true raw input so it feels way too smooth and artificial, completely unbalanced guns, a lack of gun class restrictions which nukes class cohesion and teamplay, a nonsensical and incomprehensibly confusing attachment system, the LACK of guns (even with all the portal guns the selection is putridly pitiful), specialists being so shoehorned and obnoxious it fully destroys the little class cohesion the game would have without them, a UI that stutters and freezes constantly while also being ugly and confusing, even the movement itself is weird and feels off how is that even possible?

2042 genuinely looks worse, plays worse, and has worse balancing while running infinitely worse than BF4.

Even BFV which I did not personally enjoy is a magnitudes better, more professionally developed game.

The game also has GENUINELY HORRENDOUS texture and baking work, my friend who does modded guns and armors for Helldivers 2 as a paid hobby does a better God damn job than whatever DICE did here.

And on top of all of this, the game corrupted my GPU drivers today, I've quite literally never had a game do that in my life...

Let's just say I'm never touching this sugary slop abortion of a game ever again.

As someone who’s played every Battlefield title since the early days, I can confidently say that Battlefield 2042 continues the franchise's legacy in all the right ways. It captures the chaos, the scale, and the dynamic combat that made me fall in love with the series in the first place.
The maps are vast and well-designed, offering room for every playstyle—from lone-wolf sniping to squad-based vehicle assaults. The gunplay feels smooth, the sound design is top-tier (as always), and the weather effects add just the right level of unpredictability.
Of course, like every Battlefield, you’ll need solid hardware to truly enjoy what this game can offer. But when it runs well, it looks and feels stunning—especially during massive 128-player battles.
If you're a long-time fan of the series, you'll feel right at home. And if you're new to Battlefield, this is a great place to start the madness. See you on the battlefield.

review:
Honestly, Halo Infinite feels like such a disappointment. The engine looks awful — everything has this cheap, plastic sheen that kills any sense of immersion. It’s like playing with action figures rather than a living, breathing world. After all these years, I expected way better.

The customization system is a huge step back from Reach. Remember how you could actually build your Spartan’s look without turning them into a walking neon billboard? Yeah, none of that here. Instead, you get these ugly, over-the-top cosmetics shoved down your throat — many locked behind grindy battle passes or insanely expensive bundles.

Speaking of the battle pass, it’s painfully slow and feels designed to squeeze you dry. The monetization is aggressive and clunky, making it clear that this isn’t about fun anymore — it’s about cash.

And the campaign? Honestly, it’s pretty forgettable. It lacks the punch and story depth of previous Halo games. Nothing really sticks with you once it’s done, which is a shame because that’s usually the series’ strong point.

review:
YES but only if you don't pay more than $20! I love Halo Infinite, and I HATE it. So much wasted potential. I never finished it. I shut it down during the Sequence "Easter eggs" hunt. I just got bored with it all. 
PROS: 
Maybe the best gun-handling and player movement responsiveness of any Halo game. It feels right. 
The Mongoose isn't as silly "light" as it's been in other Halo titles. That's a "sort of" complement. 
A lot of the Marine dialogue is really entertaining even if many time it's repeated too often.
The throwing and grappling are fun! Wish they would add a kicking option (Entropy Zero 2)
CONS: 
Sheesh, where do I start? LOL...
The other side of the gun handling - What are human weapons spitting out? BB's? Dang, talk about NERFED weapons. When I first fired up the game and realized that 343 just refuses to address this issue. Covenant weapons also suck. The weapons also sound muted and many times almost indistinguishable from one another. 
Sound continued. This game may have the worst sound design over-all from any other Halo title. 
Graphics are OK, just OK. The problem is that the graphics should have been spectacular. 343 worked on the game long enough.
"The weapon" and her "cute" behavior. That sh*t was way over done. Of course, Cortana and her "romance" with the Chief led the way! 343 Industries is female dominated so...
The story line. LOL...
The TAC map, That could have been made much more streamlined. As great as the weapons handle (despite the weakness and mediocre sound) the map interaction is just the opposite. What a clunker.
No passengers on the tank? WTF? That's pathertic. But it's OK because the Marines can apparently jump almost as high as a Spartan!

name: Halo Infinite
review:
Better than Halo 5, worse than 4. Mickey mouse halo game. Campaign is a waste of time and nothing really happens, just watch a youtube playthrough and skip through it. Somehow you can't replay the mainline campaign missions and the open world is basically empty other than cookie cutter named brutes/grunts that have a special weapon you get after killing them, basically filler fights to pad runtime. You also get missions to save teams of marines across the map, they don't help for the campaign though. They are not included in the main story, just another extra mission type to pad runtime.
 
Gameplay feels really good though but the firearms don't have that Halo sound. 

Story also is jumbled. Just like Halo 4 to Halo 5, Halo 5 to Infinites storyline is not continued. It is somewhat but it's done weird. Halo Wars 2 stuff isn't really included, the main enemy from that game is killed off screen, the Infinity is destroyed off screen basically, cortana destroyed off screen. 

Idk man, if you have gamepass give it a try, it's not a 0/10. Youll have fun playing it but it's nothing stellar. Multiplayer is somewhat fun, just don't go dropping 60 dollars on this

review:
Halo Infinite is the product of Mismanagement. 343i's dependence on Contractors resulted in probably the most inconsistent live service game possible. Yet I still find myself coming back.

Recently, the dev team has been super consistent with their content drops, and I hope they keep up the pace. I love the customization in this game, and hope the devs do more in the future to increase the flexibility of it as they have already. Things on my wishlist are providing additional customization to armor kits, and implementing cross-core wrist and utility attachments. The player customization is in a good spot right now, leagues better than where it was at launch.

The game is solid, but I can think of other games that have elements of Halo Infinite does, and executes better. And yet, I find myself coming back. Halo Infinite is the sum of it's parts. A fun arena shooter that effectively modernizes the classic Halo I grew up playing. I recommend this game to anyone that grew up playing classic Halo, or is curious to see what the old-heads are so crazy about. 

Me personally, Halo Infinite has a firm place in my game rotation.

Halo infinite is a fantastic singleplayer experience, building upon many modern FPS features that were initially introduced to the series with 4 and 5, two of my personal favourite games in the franchise despite 5's story issues. everything in infinite comes together into a cohesive, fluid gameplay experience that feels as though it was hand crafted like this without any trials or trouble. in many ways i consider infinite a better representation of what a halo game should be than any entry from 1 to 3, and it really only stops short in having a fairly limited weapon variety, as well thought out as they are. the lack of the carbine is sorely felt and i feel the railgun from halo 4 would have been a good addition, but the entire abilities and equipment system is fantastic. Characters are great, there are some genuinely great interactions and little story moments that still stick with me, and the villains manage to completely avoid being pastiches of past halo villains and really feel like a genuine, new threat with complex motivations.

review:
Halo Infinite marks a stellar comeback for the iconic franchise, blending the classic Halo formula with modern gameplay innovations to deliver a thrilling, expansive shooter experience. From the moment you step into Master Chief’s boots, the game recaptures the magic that made the series a household name while pushing the saga forward in exciting ways.

The campaign is a standout, weaving a compelling story of mystery, loyalty, and survival against the backdrop of the fractured Halo ring, Zeta Halo. The narrative balances grand sci-fi spectacle with intimate moments, deepening the bond between Master Chief and the AI companion, “The Weapon.” The open-ended level design encourages exploration and tactical freedom, making each encounter feel fresh and dynamic.

Gameplay feels smooth and responsive, retaining the satisfying gunplay Halo is known for while introducing new tools like the versatile Grappleshot, which adds verticality and creativity to combat and traversal. Enemy AI is smart and challenging, keeping battles intense without feeling overwhelming.

Multiplayer returns to form with a robust suite of modes, classic maps, and a progression system that rewards skill and persistence. The free-to-play model makes it accessible, and constant updates ensure a lively, evolving community.

Visually, Halo Infinite strikes a balance between nostalgia and modernity, with beautiful, sprawling environments and detailed character models that run smoothly even on mid-range hardware.

If there’s a minor criticism, it’s that some side missions in the campaign can feel a bit repetitive, but overall, the pace and variety keep things engaging.

In summary: Halo Infinite is a brilliant blend of nostalgia and innovation, offering an unforgettable sci-fi shooter experience that honors the legacy of the franchise while boldly looking to the future. Whether you’re a veteran Spartan or a newcomer, this game delivers epic moments at every turn.

Rating: 7/10

review:
Raft is a good game if you can power thought the first 3 hours. Meaning if your a single-player gamer, Raft will be a very frustrating experience, hostile even. I had to completely restart the first hour 3 time because I unknowingly soft-locked myself. In "Dark Souls" when you fail you know its simply because your trash. But in "Raft" its because you have no way to understand how to get to success. And a lot of that is because your expected to play with others. But the biggest disappointment is the shark (not Sharks). It needed to play more-so in to the horror of always being hunted and the sound design makes this worse. In-fact the sound design as a whole is poor, mainly to do with being attacked. But the story and area designs are good. Also wish I could increase the view distance...

I don't regret playing Raft or the money payed for it. But I am sadden that what should have been an excellent game, somehow fell this short. For me who loves this type of game, a "meh experience" is unexceptionable. So I can't recommend.

Ways to get soft-locked
1. Dieing without stored backup tools. Because you will loss them.
2. No, you can't start a new raft or build on land. No in-game reason is given.
3. Being unable to build a paddle, to push off that island you crashed into.

If you want a way to revive yourself without losing most of you stuff use "www.saveeditonline.com"
Your save file is at C:\Users\{Username}\AppData\LocalLow\Redbeet Interactive\Raft\User\User_{SteamUserID}\Player
Work out what "user" (I was 2) and change the values.
Users > 0 > Player > Health to value 1
Users > 0 > Player > Dead to value 0
After click on download at the bottom and replace the original file with the downloaded one. Restart game.

Also "https://www.raftmodding.com/" has a lot of good mods

review:
Before you download, be aware of what will happen to you when you play your first round of Smite (2/28 times): You get in a lobby with 4 random people that are now your teammates. Why? Because you dont have any friends to play with. The enemy Bakasura kills 2 of you before the first jungle camp even spawns. He proceeds to go 21/2/4 that game.  You end up with a 1/12/3 statline. You teammates flame you. You begin to question yourself if you were even fit to play with and against real people. You are starting to lose yourself. Are you frustrated? Yes, of course. Are you gonna play again? Probably. Will you have to play with 4 other people that grew up with absent parents?  Doubtless.

For real though, Smite is a fun free2play Moba with really f***ing awesome abilites that will leave you in awe when you first see them. Oneshotting people by calling the kraken from the depths with posidon or seeing the enemy gods as small as literal ants while you stomp with Cuthulus ult through their ranks just feels incredible. Also, the 3rd Person Camera seems weird at first, when you come from your typical moba such as League or Dota, but it is really not that bad. So just give it a try, its free. What more do you want?

name: World of Tanks Blitz
review:
Pretty entertaining for casual players. Faster crew member training than WoT(with or without golds). Lower xp requirements for tank research in tech trees. Faster paces of in-game experience. I think that's what "Blitz" is all about. Since it's "derived" from mobile platform(you can still play with mobile players), graphics performance can't compete with WoT but it's acceptable and getting better with every update(placebo maybe?)

Yes you can say it's a pay to win game since I can earn much more credits by playing tanks that are purchased with golds. Credits earned from those tanks can drastically accelerate your progress in techtrees. But honestly speaking, WoT and War thunder belong to that category as well. Either you spend a lot of time grinding for some particular tanks at certain levels that you're fond of, or you purchase in-game currency and speed up the process. The golds are on discount from time to time. So I'm pretty satisfied with it. 

I do hope WG can provide an exclusive HD graphics pack for PC players. The cooling fans of my gaming laptop never speed up when playing WOTB(i7-9750h+RTX 2080 max q)There're so much headroom that WOTB can squeeze out of average gaming laptop specs.

Edit(4/29/2020): 
Developers have justed added Girls und Panzer tanks in ALL SERVERS. Yes, you can buy Pz IV Ausf H, Tiger I & Hetzer that're originated from GuP TV animation. I really appreciate this decision cuz these tanks have been exclusive in Asia server for more than 4 years due to copyright reasons. Now not only can you purchase the collection in EU server(Russian server as well I guess), but two more tanks(IS-2 and Firefly) from the anime have been added to WOTB. Thx WG for showing the players and fans that you still care a lot about this project that you're in collaboration with after all these years.

name: Counter-Strike
review:
It was 2003.
I was nine years old—too young to understand recoil patterns, too young to know what "peeker's advantage" meant—but just old enough to feel the rush of a last-second defuse.

My older brother sat me down in front of our family’s bulky desktop, its fan whirring like a tired soldier. The monitor hummed, the keyboard clacked, and suddenly, I was in a world where nothing else mattered.

He loaded cs_assault, and I didn’t know the rules.
I didn’t know the callouts.
I didn’t even know which gun was "good."
But I knew the feeling—the electric jolt of a headshot, the panic of hearing footsteps behind me, the sheer weight of a round slipping away.

This wasn’t just a game.
It was a warzone where every second counted.

And then came the obsession.
The late nights spent memorizing grenade throws.
The way my hands shook clutching a cheap mouse in 1v1 clutch situations.
The maps weren’t just levels—they were battlefields I dreamed about.
I learned by dying.
By walking into my own Molotovs.
By planting the bomb in the wrong spot and getting screamed at in broken Russian over voice chat.
But every failure made me hungry.

My mother would sometimes pause in the doorway,
watching me lean closer to the screen like it might save me.
She didn’t get why I cared about terrorists and counter-terrorists.
But she let me have it—this place where skill mattered more than luck,
where every loss was a lesson, not just an ending.

Now, twenty years later, I still boot it up.
The textures are jagged.
The movement feels stiff compared to what’s out there now.
The community is a graveyard of forgotten aliases.

But something in Counter-Strike still lives.
The echo of an AK-47 bursting through a hallway.
The way your crosshair shakes when you’re the last one alive.
The maps—oh god, the maps—still humming with the ghosts of a thousand firefights.

Counter-Strike isn’t just a game.
It’s a time capsule.
A relic from when shooters weren’t about skins or ranks—
just grit, instinct, and the beautiful, brutal simplicity of outplaying someone.

And as I buy my Kevlar one more time,
as I step onto de_dust2 like it’s 2005 all over again,
I’m still there.
Fingers on WASD...
And a feeling I can’t quite place—
whether it’s longing, or just the quiet joy of coming home.

[b] Getting one for yourself? [/b] 
Don't think twice, don't even bother downloading the demo, just get the game. It is worth it and it has lots of potential in the future.

[b] Overwhelmed? [/b] 
Take your time, if you can't do it in a day, you can always continue it the next day, there is no pressure in this game.

You can gradually automate the work when you progress through the game. Enjoy the process, that is all I can tell you.

[b] Thoughts on product management [/b]
The drug management is horrible, the only thing you can do is mark a drug as favourite. Newly concocted drug is added at the end of the list, if you have experiment hundreds of them, you have to scroll all the way down. Don't even imagine I how I look up for a drug.

[spoiler] Keeping track of the drugs (especially name) isn't going to get you anywhere. The most important thing is the combination of the ingredients and the effect it causes. I also found out the price is not related to how many ingredients you put but the effect it gives. This hypothesis is validated through the Wiki (I didn't look up the combination and decided to figure it out myself, don't ruin the fun!) [/spoiler] 

[b] What are the features that could make the game play easier? [/b]

- Marking customer or taking a note (where they live, etc) on the map.
- Better product management: organize it and at least put some categorizing, grouping, filtering, or searching.
- More interaction with the people, not just offering them drugs.
- Hunger system? Limit the energy when running?

 I've used the Community setup, specifically the Loadout for PS4 controllers, however, like I said, it worked for an hour, and hasn't worked since. I don't know what to do, besides start yet another new game, and hope it works... 

This game will likely be fun, but holy, I haven't had such issues in setting up a game as much as this one. Can't wait to have the game out of early access to see how the accessibilty will hopefully address these issues for me, because as it is, I feel like a Quality Assurance Tester, only I'm not getting paid for it.

review:
TLDR: 3.8/5

To start off, I've been playing this game on/off since before official launch, I was actually a "Founder" for purchasing the founder pack waaaay long ago. It's accurate to say my experiences with this game are mostly positive, and I feel it's my duty to explain some of the points other people have in their reviews more in depth.

Starting off:

Pros: 
-Free
-Graphically flexible(can run on a bad pc or a great pc)
-Solid weapons, mechanics, etc.
-Compared to most BR games, this game still feels unique compared to others I've played.\
-Well designed maps
-Good character design


Cons:
-Bots?(see more later)
-Sometimes glitchy(mostly when jumping off high areas and trying to use the grappling hook. if the game stutters when doing this, you will die.
-Repetitive?(Usually the game is more or less locked to one map for a majority of the time, but it does change. also there are limited time game modes that appear, usually with a different map than the set map. Otherwise don't expect the set map to change more than once every season.

Now to get into some of the points up above. I'll start by saying that in addition to playing this game over a few years, currently (season 12) I've really enjoyed getting back into it and I am currently #22 in solo's in the game, so I would say its safe to say I more or less know what I'm talking about.

-Bots: I'm not too sure if they exist in the game, but I think it'd be safe to say that they do exist, and they do make the game a bit easy. I've never seen any official posts or patch notes regarding bots but I also never really kept up much with the game news since I play on/off a lot. Bots really just make the game lose appeal after a while, and as far as I can tell, it doesn't matter how good or bad you are, you might just get a game full of them, or with almost none. I'm ranked very high and I run into what I feel are bots very often. (more so in squads than in solo's) either that or the player base skill has really gone downhill.

-Desert Map/the season 10/11 catastrophe: This seems to be(from reviews/things I've heard from friends) to be pretty much the most hated map in ROE existence, but I would like to preface this saying that I've personally never played it, since I believe it was introduced in season 10 or 11, which I did not play during. Currently, in season 12, this map is not in rotation, so I have no gripes with it considering I pretty much love both the other maps. The game currently is not portrayed very well by the screenshots on steam, as almost all of them are season 11/10 which are basically widely hated(from my perspective) so I believe it is unfair to judge the game based on those few seasons/one map.

-Thoughts on current season compared to how I felt about previous seasons:
Honestly I've had a ton of fun playing this game this season, mainly because I can actually get into lobbies fairly quickly, very consistently. The main reason I played on/off was that usually the wait times for lobbies used to be extremely high(like 15 minutes to get into a game) The current season has no issues with this but I would probably attribute this due to the fact bots seem to be in the game now.
Season 1 was incredible for its time, offered a fresh new take on the BR genre and did it well. Season two introduced a new map: Europa Island, and a variety of new weapons, traversal options, customization items, etc. Season two was probably my all time favorite. Since then, I haven't noticed a whole ton of innovation to the game, as major changes only happen at the beginning of each season. The game seems to be in a state of "Return to Form" as it is fairly similar to how it was back in season 2, which I believe is probably caused from the backlash of the desert map.

In game store/loot- There are in game purchases for this game, mostly for the premium currency. Honestly, the currency is fairly cheep, and you can buy enough to get a battle pass for a whole season for about 10 bucks. The game also has another currency that you get for playing the game, ranking well, getting kills, winning etc, called coins. Coins can be used to purchase weapon skins/trinkets etc. which offers a f2p model for getting cool loot.(Although if you aren't consistently winning, farming up coins will most likely take a long time.) Otherwise, you're better off getting the battle pass, and maybe buying a few loot boxes.

Crashes/Glitches:
Throughout my time playing this game I have seen minimal issues regarding crashes/glitches. Currently, there seems to be an issue with the steam overlay being enabled, which may cause your game to crash randomly. I myself have the overlay disabled, and my game still seems to crash every once in a while. The only other gripes I have is that when jumping from high altitudes with the grappling hook, the game may stutter/glitch, and if this happens while you use your grappling hook, you will most likely die from fall damage.

I run this game at absolute maximum settings, and honestly I'd say besides COD, and maybe Apex, this game looks better than pretty much every other BR game I've ever played.

All in all, very solid game, if they marketed more, and fixed a few things, honestly it could be genre defining. There's a lot of good here, and a lot of questionable things as well, but I'll update this if anything big ever happens that I think deserves a review.

The game is constantly churning out more and more of these, without any sign of letting up, and I'm not even sure it's possible to play them all at once. 

The game is glitchy, slow, and honestly, boring. When it isn't boring, it's frustrating. 

You have to make a special account in a third party app that begged repeatedly for my address after being told no, which can't be shared to another Steam account. So if you, say, only want your child to play on an account you run and supervise, you can't do that. The app itself is a third party download probably because it's a glorified code checker, an extremely brazen attempt to prevent any eeeevil password sharing, which clearly would be bad for the Sims, since as you can see from the 2,000 USD of DLC, they're quite hard up for cash! 

It's greedy, annoying, unlikable, and irritating to play. I haven't enjoyed any of my time with it, and certainly wouldn't pay two thousand dollars for more hats and a bunch of blatant advertising deals in the form of "cross overs" or whatever. It barely runs on a standard laptop anyway, so unless you have a good gaming PC, don't bother. 

And if you do have a good gaming PC, you should consider playing a game that respects you as a player and isn't trying constantly to wring 2k out of you.

    You’ll huddle by the fire. You’ll weep for daylight.

Chaos

    The true deity.
    Deerclops at Day 29. Your base? Splinters.
    A "friendly" firefly ignites the forest.
    Your friend, starving, eats your last Pierogi.
    All is ash. All is beautiful.

☠️ SACRED SUFFERINGS (Highlights)

    *Permadeath: Watching your corpse decay as a ghost while friends ignore your woeful moans.

    *Winter: When hope freezes solid. (Also your toes.)

    *The Hounds: Hell’s doorbell. Always ringing when you’re naked and afraid.

    *Wortox: “I ate your soul. For healing. SORRYNOTSORRY.”

    *Caves: Where sanity goes to die… and depth worms throw the funeral.

⚰️ VERDICT

    10/10 WOULD STARVE AGAIN.
    This game didn’t just break me.
    It taught me the sacred geometry of panic-farming.
    It made me cherish the Goose that crushed my skull twelve times.
    It gifted me resilience (dubious), ingenuity (desperate),
    and an eternal craving for Monster Lasagna.

Now pardon me, Forsaken Ones.
The Nightmare Cycle approaches.
My Beefalo horn thirsts for another charge into oblivion.

Sorrowful be the stomach. Heavy be the log stack.
So Mote It Be. 🔥🪓

review:
Played both the main game and the DLC: The Following. 

The main game was super fun. There are multiple ways you can kill a zombie and so the combat is really satisfying. The parkour in the main game works so well, there are many buildings for you to climb and it's fun being able to kill zombies with parkour. Parkour mechanics are very satisfying as well.

Main game story was interesting, kind of predictable in some scenarios but overall a decent story.

The DLC: The Following wasn't as great as the main game because you are placed in the country side with not many buildings. You still do parkour but it's limited because you are in big fields most of the time. To get around the map, you use the Dune Buggy. The Dune Buggy is fun to drive though and you can add weapons and defence systems to it, which makes driving it even more fun.

But once you have completed the DLC: The Following, you realize the missions/quests/side quests all boil down to "go to point A, B, C, D, .... and collect X, Y, Z. You may argue that's most games. Sure but I wish there were more exploration missions/quests/side quests. Nevertheless, this isn't a big deal because at the end of the day, it's really fun to do the missions/quests/side quests as you have to get through a horde of zombies and you have to do that with combat. And as I said, combat in this game is really rewarding.

One con though is you can't play stealth in this game if you don't have a crossbow. The human enemies know exactly where you are if you get close to them, there is no way of sneaking up to them. You can sneak up to zombies though...

And this is not a con but it would have been cool if there was a sniper rifle added to the game or even a silencer, just to satisfy that itch of wanting to play stealthily for those who love playing that way.

The DLC: The Following is not a must. If you really enjoyed the main game, you will enjoy the DLC: The Following but not to the extent of the main game. It's not a Cyberpunk like DLC where it's a must play.

Other than that, I don't have anything bad to say about it, had heaps of fun.

name: Dying Light
review:
[h1]Dropkick and parkour your way through the zombie apocalypse![/h1]

[i]First-person action survival game set in a post-apocalyptic open world overrun by flesh-hungry zombies. Roam a city devastated by a mysterious virus epidemic. Scavenge for supplies, craft weapons, and face hordes of the infected.[/i]

[h2]Story & Quests[/h2]
You play as Kyle Crane, a GRE (Global Relief Effort) operative sent into Harran to recover sensitive data and assist survivors. But Crane quickly becomes entangled in the politics and morality of survival, forced to choose between duty and helping those in need.

[u]Story missions:[/u] Narratively driven, involving Crane’s role in the city’s fate.
[u]Side quests:[/u] Help survivors, clear quarantine zones, deliver drops.
[u]Random events:[/u] NPCs getting attacked, air drops landing, enemy ambushes.
[u]Safe zones:[/u] Areas you can clear and unlock to rest, store gear, and fast travel.

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
Dying Light is a first-person action survival horror game, where killing zombies is the majority of the gameplay. Melee weapons are the primary means of attack, and consist of bats, crowbars, machetes, axes, swords - most are customizable. You can also attach weapon mods that add electricity, fire, or poison effects using crafting materials. You can collect materials to craft weapons, mods, traps, throwables, lockpicks, and healing items. Weapons degrade over time, forcing you to constantly scavenge and upgrade. Firearms are available as well, but rare early on, more common later. They're powerful but noisy (attract infected). You can also use a bow that is silent and deadly.

The parkour mechanic is another major part in this game and a really cool feature. You can climb, vault, and leap across rooftops and obstacles. You can climb almost anything - walls, ledges, rooftops, lamp posts, and more. As you level up, you gain parkour moves like dropkicks, wall runs, a grappling hook, and more. Dropkicking zombies is so satisfying. Movement feels fluid and is a big part of surviving. Movement is your lifeline, especially at night when fighting is often suicide. Being good at escaping is essential.

[u]The game features three major skill trees:[/u]
[b]Survivor[/b] – Crafting, better healing, shop discounts.
[b]Agility[/b] – Parkour moves, better stamina, mobility tricks.
[b]Power[/b] – Melee strength, finishing moves, combat efficiency.

You gain XP in each category based on what you do. Climbing boosts agility, fighting boosts power, etc. You also level up Crane’s gear: new blueprints, armor, and weapons.

The game can be played up to 4-player online co-op. It’s much more fun playing co-op than solo and it works really well.

[h2]Enemies & Bosses[/h2]
[u]The enemies and bosses consist of different zombies and humans:[/u]
[b]Biter[/b] - Basic zombie, slow.
[b]Viral[/b] - Faster zombie.
[b]Night Walker[/b] - Faster and more aggressive than Virals.
[b]Hazmat[/b] - Slow zombie with a gas tank on its back. 
[b]Goon[/b] - Large zombie wielding large melee weapons.
[b]Toad[/b] - Spit toxic acid from a distance.
[b]Screamer[/b] - Emit a loud scream when they see you, attracting Virals.
[b]Bomber[/b] - Bloated infected that run toward you and explode.
[b]Bolter[/b] - Flee immediately upon seeing you. Drop Bolter Tissue, used for crafting.
[b]Demolisher[/b] - Huge, tank-like infected with armor.
[b]Volatile[/b] - Ultra-aggressive night creatures.
[b]Rais' Men[/b] - Human bandits and thugs.

[h2]Environment[/h2]
The game takes place in Harran. It's an open world with a lot to do. The game has a dynamic day and night cycle. During daytime it's safer to explore, scavenge and complete missions as infected are slower and less aggressive. During nighttime zombies are more dangerous and Volatiles come out to hunt you. They are extremely fast and dangerous. You earn more XP for combat kills and agility moves. Missions become riskier but more rewarding.

The world is filled with activatable traps - car bombs, UV lights, environmental hazards - that can be used to kill zombies creatively. There are no invisible walls. If you can see it, you can probably get there.

[h2]Visual Design & Sound Design[/h2]
The game is beautifully designed. The city of Harran really looks apocalyptic. Corpses in the streets, graffiti on the walls, zombies everywhere. Harran feels like a real, decaying city under siege. The zombies and Volatiles look grotesque and intimidating. The infected don’t just look scary - they look diseased, like they’re falling apart. Melee effects are brutal where heads crack, limbs break, blood spurts.

The sound design is great. The Infected have different sound cues, which is important. Biters moan and gurgle constantly. Virals have panicked breathing or angry yelling before you see them. Volatiles have growls that are distinct and terrifying, with loud screeches when they spot you - immediate cue to run. They have heavy, thunderous footfalls - you can hear them sprinting up behind you.

Each weapon has unique sound effects: metal clanks, wood thuds, machete slashes. Hits sound crunchy and visceral - skulls crack, bones break, flesh tears.

[h2]Constructive Criticism[/h2]
While melee is the focus, gunplay is underwhelming. Weapons lack weight and aiming can feel stiff and unresponsive. Human enemies don’t offer challenging gunfights and are quite dumb many times.

Many side quests boil down to fetch quests or simple kill objectives. Boring and repetitive after a while.

The main story is formulaic and forgettable - a typical "undercover agent in a doomed city" arc. The villain Rais is generic and lacks depth - your standard violent tyrant with little motivation beyond cruelty. The final fight against Rais was a boring and annoying QTE.

[h2]The Verdict[/h2]
Dying Light is for sure one of the best co-op zombie-killing experiences out there. The melee combat is brutal and satisfying, the parkour is fun and immersive, and the world is beautiful. Despite the few flaws, Dying Light is a thrilling and addictive survival horror game that shines brightest when you’re running for your life, dropkicking zombies off rooftops, and barely escaping the night.

[h2]Rating: 9/10[/h2]

But it feels so surreal to find out how the game was before, in a more "unfinished" and "undeveloped" version, and to see how many of the features that used to exist before my time, that I (and, according to my knowledge, most of the community) consider to be straight-up upgrades to the current system, are not in the game anymore. It feels so sad to see a game, that, admittedly, still is pretty fun to play sometimes, downgrade after each update, rather than improve. It seems like such a waste, all the hours, days and years spent on developing this game, all the wonderful features that could have made this a truly great game, that could have made this THE zombie survival game, maybe even as close as we could have ever gotten to a 3D Project Zomboid, cut down and simplified. Game was pretty good right up until the 2.0 update.  2.0, however, is absolutely awful and needs to be rolled back immediately.  The <only> positive that I have for the patch is they seem to have upped the "honey" drop rate from stumps, making early game infection less awful.

That said, the different biomes are now "gated", you need to have some special drink in order to survive in them, which, that's stupid.  The biomes have different environmental effects as well, with the burned forest giving you a 3 minute timer before you start taking smoke inhalation damage (mitigated if you had your special smoothie beforehand), and fully mitigated (I think?) if you wear a set of non-primitive armor and get a magical badge that protects from smoke.  That part is broken though, wearing armor that I looted didn't give me the achievement, and I can't make any because armor crafting is gated behind what books drop for you.  

So yeah, new version you have a heat stroke and start dying if you step into a desert for 2 minutes.  You start freezing to death in 30 seconds in the snow.  You are stuck in a tiny fraction of the map before you jump through arbitrary hoops that make no sense and are also apparently locked behind a combination of RNG and bugs.  

Then there are the new biome zombies.  So far the most annoying I have found is the desert one, that attacks from a distance with an insect swarm that you might be able to outrun, but also slows you down and gives you about 5% disease with each hit.  Wandering into the desert for the first time, got hit by three of them at the same time.  Completely wiping out your supply of antibiotics in a matter of seconds isn't really compelling gameplay.

I dont understand the determination from the devs to rip all creativity out of this game. Devs that embrace cheese and mods make better games. They did there live before the launch and said they listen to the community ad long as what theyre saying what the devs are thinking and what the devs business goals are lmao. Their determination to destroy this game is unrivaled. 

The game is like Minecraft and day Z. It is glitchey and janky and thats what used to make it fun. But every time you find a way to play the game your own way, a way the devs dont like or think is the way you should be playing the game, they remove the feature. Sometimes within 24 hours if its popular enough on a sub. Absurd and shameful. Look at speed runners, thats not a way the devs expected the game to be played but its fun and people look for glitches to exploit for a challenge after enjoying the game and story initially. If I buy a game and beat it and then decide to play it however I want it shouldn't crack the fragile ego of a dev that they have to patch it out. 

The DLC is a joke. Some cosmetic stuff. Skins for actual dollars is like begging. Just put it in the game. Make more ways to build and make bases, every base shouldn't look the same. A path up for the zombies, a pole path for them to get to you in a secured room so you can cap them in a line or hit with a melee. We should be free to play it HOWEVER we want, and embrace the exploits. If we want to kill an animal to distract during horse night or drive around we should be able to.

The 2.0 update is a joke. Theyre forcing biome progression rather than just giving benefits or features of staying in a particular biome through level progression. The forced tasks to unlock the next biome are weak. Make a couple drinks, go into the biome with a buff to not get hurt by the conditions of the biome, collect all you need and poof now you dont need the drink lol. The locust zombie is annoying, it spans more than any other zombie and the swarm is a power hit away from disappearing. It should be harder. The yeti I ran into day 1 with a bone knife successfully. I loved this game, and now I cant play it without mods. 

If youre comfortable using mods, then you can find ways to make this game fun. If youre not, this game will be fun for a bit, but in my opinion not enough for the price tag. I hope someone learns from where these devs went wrong and make a new game and does the opposite of what they did.

name: 7 Days to Die
review:
Writing this review after The Fun Pimps released version 2.0 for 7 Days to Die. Do not buy this game. Pick up the game now and you'll probably have a good time but come back in 6 months and you won't.

The developers have continued to make it clear they do not care about their communities and will change this game to force you to play it the way they want you to. This is a 2.0 update that is continuing to majorly rework aspects of the game despite no longer being in Early Access. Changes that sound cool on the surface such as a storm system unique to each biome are poorly implemented solely to hinder the player's exploration and fun. Want to explore harder biomes for better loot? Sorry! All we can give you is UI HUD effects and damage over time to force you to go through them in a specific order.

I enjoyed this game for years while it was in early access because it is fun to explore and scavenge a zombie apocalypse to prepare for an inevitable horde night. However, with every update they have struggled to further improve this experience with new weapons, vehicles, traps, etc and instead try their hardest to force players to engage with their grindy, unrewarding leveling system, painfully repetitive quest system, and 1 dimensional dungeon exploration.

Everything said here is on top of an addition to 2.0 being DLC cosmetics. Single outfits for 10 dollars is a disgustingly greedy ask especially when you charge 45 dollars for a game that will stutter every 5 seconds. The Fun Pimps will continue to price gouge this buggy, unoptimized game and make anti-fun and anti-player changes instead of fixing its problems and adding new interactive content.

Do not buy this game! These people do not deserve your money and will spit on you for even voicing your opinion by turning off comments and ignoring you. The state of this game is inexcusable after being in development for 15 years. The Fun Pimps can say all they want about "Game development is hard. No other game is like this blah blah blah" but all these systems have been seen in other games and have been done better and more competently. Save your money and don't support these developers.

name: 7 Days to Die
review:
I own both the Xbox version (support ended years ago) and the PC version, so it'd be a lie to say that I don't enjoy the game. Although, I've gotta say that this new update SUCKS. The future direction of the game is looking dire and the newly introduced DLC cosmetics raise some flags with how the "Fun" Pimps will decide to approach micro-transactions in the future. 

With that said, my biggest grievances with the update are primarily regarding the Biome Progression & Storm System. 

Biome progression - Seems like an attempt to make the game more immersive and WHILE ITS NOT A HORRIBLE IDEA, the execution of this new mechanic is poor and ironically immersion breaking. It adds a list of chores to complete that impede your progress with no real pay-off. Not only is Biome Progression a waste of your time, but also it just doesn't make any sense. Scoutmaster Rekt must've been teaching players how to breathe through their backsides considering how you somehow become completely impervious to the harmful effects of continuous smoke inhalation, but why question it since you got a sweet boy scout badge to go with it. Wonder how they explain immunity to radiation poisoning later on. 

Instead, what should have been done is have traders offer special quests or leads on where to find special equipment that allow you to endure the effects of each biome. For example, one of the traders offers you a lead on the location of a military base where medical testing was conducted during the initial outbreak with the end loot granting you a guaranteed hazmat suit. The special equipment itself could take a mod slot and adds a layer of depth to the game without sacrificing immersion. 

Storm System - Again like Biome Progression, the Storm System isn't a bad idea but also suffers from poor execution. The only ways to negate the effect of the storms is by finding shelter or outright leaving the biome which is just, for lack of a better term, boring. The weather/temperature/climate hasn't really had any impact on gameplay for a LONG time with the effects of temperature fluctuations being incredibly easily to brush off and ignore (I bet some people reading probably don't even notice these effects in-game). And for some reason, the whole "Storm Brewing" update does NOTHING to expand on these features or utilize existing/old ones to enhance the Storm System that was added. For instance, the perk "Well Insulated" was removed in 2.0 and I guarantee that ~80% or more of players have no idea what this perk does or have never put a point into it once. Why? Because it was useless since climate changes and temperature fluctuations aren't noticeable outside of the visual/atmospheric changes that accompany them. So why add a Storm System and then remove a perk related to enduring various climates and harsh weather conditions? It feels like a massive lost opportunity to improve on the game's existing features and mechanics and is very disheartening as someone who really enjoys this game. And it doesn't stop there, the "Cooling Mesh Mod" and the "Insulated Liner Mod" are two armor mods that protect against harsh weather but were, for some reasons, removed when the Sh*t Brewing update came out. Make it make sense please. 

One might argue that "if you don't like it, then you can just turn it off. Stop making a big deal out of it." - Okay, but why even add these features into the game then? It's almost as if the developers know that what they're bringing to the dinner table is a pile of hot garbage, but they make it "okay" by saying we don't have to eat it if we don't want to. THATS SUPER LAME. We don't get major updates frequently, so its a kick in the teeth to half the players who don't like the update because we want to join in on the fun too. Again, why bother adding stuff into the game and then giving us the option to never interact with it? It just seems like a waste of time and resources that could've been spent improving existing issues or re-working irrelevant perks and so on. 

Regarding the DLC cosmetics, while no one is forcing myself or anyone else to buy them, they are just another kick in the teeth to those who are unhappy about this update (especially for older players). From my point of view, this update is overall like a 3/10 and for the developers to have the audacity to charge almost $10 for silly cosmetics is nefarious, not even Reverse Flash is that devious. The game already lacks features for character customization but it just makes things worse when you now A LOT of cosmetics were actually removed a while ago (there used to be 8-10 outfit slots/a lot more clothing). Overall, I'm against the Cosmetic DLCs mainly because they removed the entirety of the old cosmetics that were completely free and are implementing paid cosmetics when customization features are already pretty much nonexistent (maybe because they removed them lol).

Let's be honest, majority of the "good" things about this update were Quality of Life (QOL) changes that should've been expected to be added into the game at some point. It is genuinely crazy to me that some people (NOT EVERYONE) who have positive opinions on this update refer to the QOL changes as the best parts... brother you need to raise your standard cuz they out here BARELY doing the bare minimum. 

Not uncommon "Fun" Pimps L. Will be playing the previous version IF things get better.

Overall, it’s a great survival game once you get over the initial hump — but the early experience could definitely use some balance.

I play games to escape adult life, why would I want to do chores??? And why would I pay nearly $10 for an armor skin???? Idk man... I am sad to say I agree with a LOT of the negative reviews being given to the game lately. I wanted to believe it wasnt true, but this game is going way downhill. Not to mention they made all these negative changes on TOP of increasing their game cost to $45.00US which is a BONKERS cost for this game. review: Excellent single player experience with counter strike gunplay. For anyone who hasn't played this you absolutely should. Highest difficulty is not too hard and is the correct way to experience the game. If you are going to play this game be aware that the game (at least for me) is bugged in that you can't actually continue playing the game after a certain point in the first level. The game will kick you out of the level and send you back to the main menu. In order to fix this you need to opt-in to the "beta-beta" build of this game. Right click the game in your library and click on "properties". This opens up a new window. Click on "Betas", then "Beta Participation" and then "beta-beta". This allowed me to actually play the game. It will also make your Counter Strike (1.6) and HL1 versions switch to their beta's as well. This broke CS 1.6 for me, but after you finish CSCZDS you can revert it back to its regular version.

name: Counter-Strike: Condition Zero
review:
A great game, I've got to say.

I wasn't expecting much from this game, but it turned out to be a pleasant surprise. It has some solid mechanics for its time, and while the story is short and has no continuity, it's still a lot of fun, it's got a lot of clever little parkour puzzles. Although I have to admit, I almost rage quit during some missions. My main complaint with the game is that enemies seem to track you through walls the spawn rate is pretty overkill and enemies you've already killed will oftentimes respawn in cleared areas during certain mission phases. Plus you always have to be careful with your ammo because it runs out very fast often leaving you with just your secondary weapon(if you're lucky) or even your knife.

Overall, it's a great game and a solid Counter Strike story mode if you ask me. Too bad it got lost in the shuffle and never got the attention it deserved.

name: Counter-Strike: Condition Zero
review:
Note: This review is primarily about the deleted scenes portion of the game, which if you're here its most likely because you heard CS:CZ was a campaign mode entry into the series. That part is Counter Strike: Condition Zero Deleted Scenes which comes with the main game (which is basically just 1.6 with fairly impressive ai for the time), Its the one you would want to play however I wouldn't really recommend it. 

On paper it seems dope, but maaaan does it have a lot of stuff holding it back. To start the game is just fragmented missions. No connecting story line at all. You are given an world map and take the role of different spec ops teams from around the globe (even Russia which is interesting to see them portrayed as good guys from a western developer). You never play as the terrorists which sucks since its half of CS' identity. 

Since you aren't here for the story, is the gameplay and level design any good at least? Ehhhhh... while the game is built on source, an engine dear to my heart and one renowned for its interesting physics. It has been completely gutted here, patching out fun mechanics like bhopping making the boring level design even more prominent. Did I mention the levels completely blow? Ok that's not all true, some are really interesting! Pretty much every level designed by Russell Meakim has an interesting setting combined with a good selection of weapons. However even these fall victim to some noticeable design flaws. I played all levels at max difficulty, which revealed how poorly placed enemies can be. Sometimes they mimic real CS being tucked in tight corners that you have to clear on entries. This is fine however often they can be placed at the start and ends of ladders and climbing objects. If you've ever played CS you'd know this is fucked up. So whenever I got on a ladder I would get one-tapped (due to high difficulty) with no way to defend myself. My skills aren't being tested here, just my patience.

Anyways some are worth playing some are pretty bad filler, if you're super curious I'd say give it a go. If anything atleast you get the wildest credit scene to send you out. 

Oh and also Ig its a product of the time but this game fetishizes asian women quite a bit so.. yeah

4/10

name: eFootball
review:
This is obviously the worst PES game I've ever played. But it shows that Konami wants to get away from the recycle-old-game-and-stick-a-new-name-on scheme. Some ideas and approaches are very good (more movements without the ball, cross-play, transitionless corners and throw-ins, etc...), but the implementation is very miserable. To be honest, even old functions that have always worked flawlessly are miserable now. In the end, this just shows how hard it actually is to bring a completely new game to market instead of remarketing the same game for full price. I like the approach of putting more effort into the football games, bringing new features and taking risks. It's a shame that PES flopped this year, but since it's free, you shouldn't bitch so much. Kudos to Konami for daring to make this right step. I'll wait for EFootball until it's ready.

Edit.

The updated version of EFootball is not comparable to the beta version which was very criticized. The game runs very smoothly and I hardly had any bugs, the graphics and animations look very realistic especially on high graphics settings. The game dynamics are rarely disturbed by fading to freekicks or throw-ins, the game continues to run while the players are getting the ball ready, which is very good. When there are cut scenes they are well used and hardly interfere. It feels more like watching a game on TV.
The game dynamics have also improved a lot, offensive players move smartly and the defense also makes few mistakes. In order to get a goal situation you have to either trick the opponent to open up passing situations or outplay the opponent with well-directed passes. At the moment, besides the friendly matches and online games, there is only the Dream Team mode, where you create and manage a team online and play against the AI or online games. It is good that you can buy the standard players directly and do not have to pull from "packs". These then start at level 0 and you have to level them up to their normal value and then you can go a bit beyond that. Very good I found here the possibility that you can choose the value upgrades yourself and thus can form your perfect player. You can e.g. skill MBappe to be more focused on speed and dribbling to let him play more on the wing or increase the values for finishing and attacking to set him up as a center forward. The choice is up to you. Since Efootball is free, there is a fear that the game will become pay-to-win. So far, however, I have been able to do well with my non-pay-to-win team and have not had the feeling that I had a big disadvantage compared to the other players. The good thing is that Featured players and the "normal form" of the same players usually have the same values when they are at the highest level. Featured players just start at a higher value and don't need to level up as long. Also, Featured players often have an alternate focus on skills. Only some legend players that are hard to get are a lot better than the "normal" counterparts. I would have been happy if legendaries had been just as good and you only acquired them, for example, if you were a big fan, so as not to break the balance of the game. But so far opponents had only 2-3 legends in the team and the difference was not so big that you have no chance against them.

All in all, I think the game is good, it's fun and brings a lot of new features. But some corners must still be tweaked.

review:
WARNING: DO NOT WASTE A SINGLE CENT ON THIS GAME. Let it resolve its issues (current version is v0.9, so...) and come check after a while. Perhaps on black friday... If you don't play online, stick with 2021 and install a mod.

Now, on to more detailed feedback. Veteran since PES 3 with Collina on the cover, so I skipped the first match because the game wasn't allowing me to change the control settings. With that problem solved on the main menu, I played two games. One online, then one offline. No issue online, took a bit to find to an opponent but I think is rather normal at this time... 
It is a TOTAL revamp. You really can't even identify anything from eFootball PES 2021. Playability is rather realistic, in an awful way. I simply hate it. It’s no FIFA, but it’s not good either. The player drifts like crazy and controlling the ball gets more complicated each year, needs more and more input. You either use like five fingers to make it do what you want or you loosing control of the ball is a rather realistic result. Tacking and pressuring also seems to be getting hard by the year and it achieved another level with this game. 

Menus are completely different and a bit confusing, but with some extra features. Still, its presentation is very basic, hopefully with more game features coming out, that will improve. Training, on the other hand, went from a full feature to a video… Gosh! -_-‘

It really feels like a new game from scratch, thus the number of bugs already identified. KONAMI should paid some of the money back. They just released the game and that's it. I paid 40€ for this premium thing, and yet it feels like I'm apart of some sort of beta testing... Honestly, what a waist of (my) money.

In short:
The first release was still too early in my opinion. Though the roadmap, which has been public for a while now, does clearly state that some of the main content will be provided as updates until early next year. 
Beside this and a few flaws here and there, it is fun to play. Physics and flow etc. are already much better than in comparable games (e.g. F..A). Though there is still room for improvement. As there has been in PES in the past. 
In the end a no-brainer for me.

For all players with negative reviews:
Check your graphics settings in game! 
I have no problem with 4K@120, it's running buttery smooth (RTX 3090).
Since the engine changed, there are many graphics options compared to the past versions.
If your graphics card does not provide enough power, it can be stuttery as hell.

review:
So, this project started out as a 3D version of the successful game "Hooligansgame" made by a Polish company in Łódź, who were also known to release "Ultras Online" back in the day. The developers of THIS game wanted to piggyback off their success but became a sad attempt after all, starting out under the name of "Hooligan fighters", later "Hooligan Warriors" naturally the people expected the developers to add actual club insignia and perhaps an overworld. When the developers realized it was too much work, they gave up on the concept, made it a generic fighting game and renamed it "Street Warriors online", which already in itself tells you how much they care about their fanbased compared to how much they only care about a quick buck.

While they did put some effort in motion tracking to make the fighting moves realistic and while the maps are beautifully designed I really, really urge you not to play this game due to the developer's crappy mentality that only goes after money, unwilling to listen to any feedback the users give them. Believe me, I gave them a shot, I tried to make them listen but to no avail. The fighting in itself is really generic, stale and requires no skills at all. And instead of doing something about it, the developers, yet again, fail to listen to constructive criticism and instead make a salty post on Facebook simply calling everyone a hater and begging people for thumbs up.

Rating: 4/10

Z1 Battle Royale (formerly H1Z1) was once the king of battle royale games, inspiring the entire genre before games like PUBG, Fortnite, and Apex Legends took over. Released as H1Z1 in 2015, it had a fast-paced, arcade-style approach to battle royale, with fun gunplay, intense fights, and smooth vehicle mechanics. However, due to developer mismanagement, failed updates, and a declining player base, the game lost its identity and never fully recovered.

What Made It Great? (Back in the Day)
🔫 Fast-Paced, Fun Gunplay
Unlike PUBG’s realistic shooting, Z1 Battle Royale had a more arcade-like combat system, where movement, aim, and positioning mattered most. The snappy gunplay and quick fights made for a highly competitive experience, attracting many hardcore players.

🚗 Awesome Vehicle Combat
Z1 introduced cars and driving mechanics that felt smooth and responsive, making chases and escapes some of the most exciting moments in battle royale history. The introduction of police cars, jeeps, and off-road vehicles added depth to gameplay.

🏆 One of the First Battle Royale Games
Long before PUBG and Fortnite, H1Z1 pioneered the last-man-standing formula. It was a Twitch favorite in its prime, with huge tournaments and a thriving esports scene.

🤝 Strong Competitive Scene (For a While)
At its peak, H1Z1 Pro League had top esports teams and players competing in high-stakes matches. It was one of the first battle royales to feature ranked matchmaking and skill-based leaderboards.

What Went Wrong?
❌ Too Many Bad Updates
The developers made drastic changes to the gameplay that alienated the core player base. Updates ruined the gun mechanics, movement, and vehicle handling, turning a once-loved game into a frustrating mess.

❌ Name Changes and Identity Crisis
The game went through too many rebrands:

H1Z1: King of the Kill
H1Z1
Z1 Battle Royale
Each version tried to "fix" the game, but instead, it lost players and direction with every update.
❌ Player Base Collapse
At its peak, H1Z1 had over 100,000 concurrent players. Now, finding a match is nearly impossible due to the drastic decline in population. Most players have moved on to PUBG, Fortnite, or Warzone.

❌ Competitors Did It Better
When PUBG came out, it offered better gunplay and realism. When Fortnite launched, it brought fun building mechanics and a casual-friendly style. Z1 Battle Royale failed to keep up, and players abandoned it for better alternatives.

Conclusion
Once a trailblazer in battle royale gaming, Z1 Battle Royale (H1Z1) has now become a ghost town, abandoned due to bad updates, poor decisions, and stronger competition. While it deserves credit for inspiring the genre, it’s hard to recommend in 2025, as matches are difficult to find, and the gameplay is not what it once was.

Rating: 4/10 – A battle royale pioneer that lost its way. Play only for nostalgia, but don’t expect much.

name: Hunt: Showdown 1896
review:
A bit of a dated review, but when I initially played the game, it was (and continues to be) a very unique approach to PvPvE. While there may be things that could feel old within the game with the current mechanics, there are aspects of it that are fantastic and, after a while, you wish were in other online games. One of such things is the fact that *everything* makes a noise in this game. The only way you can't make any noise is by standing still and doing absolutely nothing. There are ways (if you progress with a particular character aka hunter) to reduce/nullify the noise you make but you gotta make it alive before you can--otherwise you have to start over with that hunter.

The addition of the map in Colorado (with mountains, different environment/trees/views, and verticality), makes a great (relative) variety of maps. They aren't a lot of maps but you'll still spend a lot of time just trying to remember a lot of the different locations within each map as they've put a lot of effort into the design of each compund. The newly-upgraded DeSalle map is fantastic with an extra brush of color compared to the classic version and makes it feel newer.

Crytek continues to make updates to the game to tweak on certain things plus frequent events. I wish they'd sometimes take some liberty to be more experimental more often, but they try to tackle some high-priority feedback from the community as they can. I'm assuming they are a much smaller team right now compared to their top Crysis days, so they may not be able to move faster in terms of their roadmap. If you can get used to the aggressive learning curve at first, you may end up appreciating the unique elements of the game such as its weapons with tons of details with different properties and pros/cons, lower rate of fire, among other things such as a (potentially) slower approach to locations, playing the "hunting" game as you track down other players, the overall ambient sounds/atmosphere, etc. You have to have a good idea on how to approach the game and may be worthwhile looking up some entry-level tips by more experienced players beforehand, but this is a good game turned fantastic if you get to play with 1 or 2 other friends (you can play in 1-, 2-, or 3-player teams).
